#!/usr/bin/python
import os, sqlite3
base = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
db = sqlite3.connect(os.path.join(base, 'catalog.db'))
db.execute('UPDATE schema_version SET version=2')
db.commit()
db.execute('ALTER TABLE products ADD COLUMN price_cents INTEGER NOT NULL')
db.commit()
db.close()

commands.command:
cd /srv/legacy2/transactional-schema-upgrade && printf '%s\n' 'repeat_run:' && ./bin/upgrade.py && printf '%s\n' 'database_state:' && python3 - <<'PY'
import sqlite3
con=sqlite3.connect('catalog.db')
print('integrity=%s' % con.execute('PRAGMA integrity_check').fetchone()[0])
print('version=%s' % con.execute('SELECT version FROM schema_version').fetchone()[0])
print('products_sql=%s' % con.execute("SELECT sql FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name='products'").fetchone()[0])
print('columns=%r' % [(r[1], r[2], r[3], r[4], r[5]) for r in con.execute('PRAGMA table_info(products)')])
print('rows=%r' % (con.execute('SELECT id, description, price_cents FROM products ORDER BY id').fetchall(),))
try:
    con.execute('UPDATE products SET price_cents=-1 WHERE id=1')
except sqlite3.IntegrityError as exc:
    print('negative_price_rejected=%s' % exc)
else:
    raise SystemExit('ERROR: negative price was accepted')
finally:
    con.rollback()
print('rows_after_constraint_test=%r' % (con.execute('SELECT id, description, price_cents FROM products ORDER BY id').fetchall(),))
con.close()
PY
